correctness.rationale: For any putative bound K<n/4, each unit-edge image admits a unique signed shortest arc. Its sum gives an integral cycle degree. In one retraction step the changed set is a union of intervals; each boundary contribution is a closed four-arc walk with total absolute length ≤4K<n and hence zero winding. Degrees cannot change from constant (0) to identity (1). All map norms are integers because edges determine the Lipschitz norm, forcing K≥ceil(n/4). The quarter-anchor parent construction has four gaps each ≤ceil(n/4), and explicit analysis of the first three and all later prefixes proves the matching upper bound. Edge and commutation checks were executed for n=3,...,128.

value.rationale: The optimal uniform retractional-filtration constant is a natural quantitative invariant controlling projection norms of Lipschitz-free retractional bases. The exact universal formula grows linearly with circumference, covers all cycle lengths instead of isolated small examples, and identifies both an explicit sharp filtration and a topological integer-degree obstruction. The four-quarter threshold is structural rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; the result does not claim novelty or optimality for unrestricted Schauder bases.
